name: Question 3
problem:
Which of the following integrals evaluates to zero due to symmetry?

- ${\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /4}{sin}^{5}⁡x\,\text{d}x$
- ${\int }_{-2}^{2}({x}^{3}+{x}^{5})\,\text{d}x$
- ${\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2}{x}^{7}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)\,\text{d}x$
worked_solution:
Recall the following:

- a function $f(x)$ is *even* if $f(-x)=f(x)$

- a function $f(x)$ is *odd* if $f(-x)=-f(x)$

Moreover, for any odd function $f(x),$ the graph of $y=f(x)$ has rotational symmetry of order $2$ about the origin, so we have

$$
{\int }_{-a}^{a}f(x)\,\text{d}x=0.
$$

So, to determine which integrals evaluate to $0$ due to symmetry, we have to determine which integrands are odd functions.

- The function $f(x)={sin}^{5}⁡x$ is an odd function, but integral I is not of the form ${\int }_{-a}^{a}f(x)\,\text{d}x$ since the upper and lower limits are not opposites. Therefore, we cannot use symmetry to simplify the integral.

- The function $g(x)={x}^{3}+{x}^{5}$ is an odd function:

$$
\begin{aligned}g(-x) & =(-x)^{3}+(-x)^{5} \\  & =-{x}^{3}+(-{x}^{5}) \\  & =-{x}^{3}-{x}^{5} \\  & =-({x}^{3}+{x}^{5}) \\  & =-g(x)\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by symmetry, we can conclude that

$$
{\int }_{-2}^{2}({x}^{3}+{x}^{5})\,\text{d}x=0.
$$

- The function $h(x)={x}^{7}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)$ is an odd function:

$$
\begin{aligned}h(-x) & =(-x)^{7}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5(-x)) \\  & =-{x}^{7}\operatorname{cos}⁡(-5x) \\  & =-{x}^{7}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x) \\  & =-h(x)\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by symmetry, we can conclude that

$$
{\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2}{x}^{7}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)\,\text{d}x=0.
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "II and III only."

  • a function f(x) is odd if f(−x)=−f(x)

Moreover, for any odd function f(x), the graph of y=f(x) has rotational symmetry of order 2 about the origin, so we have ∫−aaf(x)dx=0.

So, to determine which integrals evaluate to 0 due to symmetry, we have to determine which integrands are odd functions.

  • The function f(x)=sin5⁡x is an odd function, but integral I is not of the form ∫−aaf(x)dx since the upper and lower limits are not opposites. Therefore, we cannot use symmetry to simplify the integral.

  • The function g(x)=x3+x5 is an odd function: g(−x)=(−x)3+(−x)5=−x3+(−x5)=−x3−x5=−(x3+x5)=−g(x)✓ Therefore, by symmetry, we can conclude that ∫−22(x3+x5)dx=0.

  • The function h(x)=x7cos⁡(5x) is an odd function: h(−x)=(−x)7cos⁡(5(−x))=−x7cos⁡(−5x)=−x7cos⁡(5x)=−h(x)✓ Therefore, by symmetry, we can conclude that ∫−π/2π/2x7cos⁡(5x)dx=0.

Therefore, the correct answer is "II and III only."
